summary: An investigation now has somewhere to live. A CASE FILE collects the footage, the recorded sightings and the operator's notes for one incident in one place: bookmark the moment you are watching straight off the Timeline (on every camera on screen at once, which is what an incident usually looks like), add a sighting from Object Search, annotate each piece of evidence with why it matters, hand the case to a colleague, and close it with a stated outcome that is required rather than optional. The whole case exports as ONE verifiable file: every clip joined without re-encoding, a manifest naming each source segment and its SHA-256 alongside any period inside a clip that has no recording, the case's own audit trail as a chain-of-custody CSV, and a plain-text note explaining how to check all of it with standard tools. If a piece of evidence has no footage left, the bundle is still produced and that clip is listed as missing with the reason, because an export that quietly dropped it would look complete. The part that makes a case worth opening rather than a memo: WHILE A CASE IS OPEN, THE FOOTAGE ITS EVIDENCE POINTS AT IS NOT DELETED. Retention, the per-camera 'Purge now' and the automatic clean-up that runs when the disk fills all refuse to destroy it, including the recorder's own file sweep, which deletes by filename and knows nothing about the database. On an appliance keeping seven days of video, a case opened today would otherwise be a list of broken links next week, and nothing about the case would have changed to say so. The case screen states what it is holding, how much disk that is, and how many of those clips are only still present BECAUSE the case is open; closing the case restates that number before it releases them. Secure wipe, factory reset and deleting a camera still destroy footage regardless — a case is not a lock against the operations whose whole purpose is destruction. A second, unrelated gap this closed: the operator role could START an evidence export and could not download it. Bundles are built asynchronously, and the grant carried POST only, so the capability the role model describes as 'may export footage, may not delete it' was unusable for the role it was written for. Benching this against a recorder holding real footage turned up four more things worth stating, three of which were fixes to code that already shipped. An evidence bundle is whole stored recordings joined together, so asking for eighteen seconds hands over the minute they sit inside — and until now nothing in the bundle said so, leaving anyone who read timestamps by counting from the first frame of the video wrong by the difference. The footage is still not cut (a cut lands on the nearest keyframe rather than the moment asked for, and handing over less than was recorded is the worse answer), but every bundle now states when its video actually starts and ends, how many seconds it holds, and how far into the file the requested moment begins, in the manifest and in plain words in the verification note. The chain of custody now ends with the export itself rather than one event before it. A case bundle can no longer be collected through the single-clip download route, which a different permission governs, and export links are no longer guessable from the time they were created. And a piece of evidence bookmarked across the moment a camera came back — some of it recorded, some of it before recording began — is no longer reported as having no footage at all; it plays from the first frame that exists and says when the recording starts.
compatibility: Purely additive. Two new database tables (case_file and case_item, auto-migrated — no manual migration step) and no changes to any existing table. Cases are a new grantable PAGE: the built-in operator role receives it, viewers do not, and a custom role gets it only when an administrator grants it. Deleting a case remains administrator-only because no grantable level carries the DELETE verb. The evidence-export grant widens from POST to GET+POST for the operator role, which is the fix described above rather than a new capability. Existing installs are unaffected until somebody opens a case: with no open cases, every footage-deletion path behaves exactly as before. The footage hold fails closed — if the open cases cannot be read, a purge keeps the footage and logs why, rather than treating an error as 'nothing is held'. The evidence manifest gains four fields describing the exported video's own span; nothing was removed or renamed, so an existing reader of manifest.json keeps working. Export ids change shape (a random suffix is appended) — they are opaque and short-lived, and nothing stores them.
